title: Raising actionable written feedback on workplace-based assessments in an internal medicine residency: a quality improvement project
abstract: Problem: about one in four written comments on the residency's workplace-based assessment forms was actionable. Interventions: relabelled then split feedback prompts, micro-teaching at faculty meetings and monthly individual reports, tested in three PDSA cycles. Measures: weekly proportion of 25 sampled comments meeting three criteria on a run chart, with a gender breakdown and balancing measures. Results will be reported after March 2027.
introduction: Written comments on workplace-based assessments are often generic, residents rarely use them, and women residents receive vaguer comments. Single changes to forms or teaching have helped elsewhere but faded without reinforcement.
methods: Model for Improvement with eight baseline weeks and three cycles. Comment text was rated without dates or names by two chief residents using a three-criterion checklist, with 20 percent double rating. Run chart rules were fixed before baseline. The project was determined to be quality improvement.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the annotated run chart, the gender breakdown, rater agreement and the balancing measures.
discussion: The discussion will interpret any shift against the run chart rules and co-interventions, compare the size and durability of change with the retrieved reports, and state what the program keeps.
limitations: Single program; raters could sometimes infer the period; the outcome measures comment quality, not resident performance.
conclusion: To be written after the final cycle; limited to comment quality in this program.
summary: SQUIRE-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
